claims.evidence_quote: Overall, all models that reuse their blocks lead to results similar to those of the conventional models while requiring a much smaller model size, making them more amenable to deployment on edge devices.

survey_notes: Audio source separation instance of looping for parameter efficiency plus adaptive exit; also proposes progressive block-wise training to save memory, a training alternative to BPTT. Code URL appears with spaces in the extracted text.

title: A Generic Network Compression Framework for Sequential Recommender Systems
relevance_reason: ALBERT-style cross-layer/cross-block and adjacent-layer/block parameter sharing in a CNN sequential recommender for compression.
one_sentence: CpRec compresses NextItNet-style sequential recommenders with block-wise adaptive embedding decomposition and layer-wise parameter sharing (cross-layer, cross-block, adjacent-layer, adjacent-block), reaching 4-8x compression while usually matching or beating the uncompressed model.
key_contributions: Three new layer-wise sharing schemes beyond ALBERT's cross-layer sharing for dilated-CNN recommenders.
Observation that full cross-layer sharing significantly hurts recommendation accuracy, while adjacent sharing preserves it.
Combination with block-wise adaptive decomposition of input/softmax matrices.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: four real-world sequential recommendation datasets
setup.loops_train: fixed depth with shared layers
setup.baselines: uncompressed NextItNet

claims.claim: Full ALBERT-style cross-layer sharing significantly degrades recommendation accuracy, motivating adjacent-layer/block sharing.
claims.evidence_quote: we notice that the performance significantly decreased in both the original paper and our recommendation task by using the cross-layer sharing scheme.

claims.claim: CpRec achieves 4-8x compression and in most cases outperforms the uncompressed model.
claims.evidence_quote: we demonstrate that the proposed CpRec can achieve up to 4∼8 times compression rates in real-world SRS datasets. Meanwhile, CpRec is faster during training & inference, and in most cases outperforms its uncompressed counterpart.

survey_notes: Recsys lineage for weight sharing as compression; finds full tying hurts while partial (adjacent) tying helps, consistent with the 'partial sharing' design choice in language (e.g., relaxed recursive transformers) and with bViT's narrow-width failure.

title: ODE-Based Transformer Decoders for Iterative Sign Language Translation
relevance_reason: Iterative refinement decoder for sign language translation where each refinement step's residual update is replaced by Runge-Kutta integration (extra function evaluations of the same block).
one_sentence: Replaces the residual updates of an iterative-refinement Transformer decoder for sign language translation with RK-2/RK-4 integration, reusing the same decoder function several times per step; RK-2 beats the IPSLT baseline on PHOENIX14T and CSL-Daily with fewer decoder layers/iterations on CSL-Daily.
key_contributions: ODE view of iterative refinement decoders; higher-order Runge-Kutta updates with no added decoder parameters.
Results on PHOENIX14T and CSL-Daily with FLOPs and latency reporting against IPSLT.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: PHOENIX14T, CSL-Daily
setup.loops_train: refinement count K (e.g., 3) with RK stages
setup.baselines: IPSLT with same visual backbone

claims.claim: RK-2 refinement beats the IPSLT iterative baseline on both benchmarks, with fewer decoder layers and refinement iterations on CSL-Daily.
claims.regime: iso_data (same backbone); compute reported per config
claims.evidence_quote: RK-2 achieves 22.96 BLEU-4 on the PHOENIX14T test set and 19.34 BLEU-4 on the CSL-Daily test set, outperforming the IPSLT baseline on both benchmarks, with fewer decoder layers and refinement iterations on CSL-Daily.

survey_notes: Peripheral: the loop is a few-step decoder refinement; relevant as an example of changing the update rule (ODE integrator) rather than the loop count, connecting to neural-ODE views of looped depth.

title: LA-Sign: Looped Transformers with Geometry-aware Alignment for Skeleton-based Sign Language Recognition
relevance_reason: Encoder-decoder looped transformer (U unique layers x L passes at constant effective depth) for skeleton sign recognition, with per-iteration hyperbolic alignment loss.
one_sentence: LA-Sign loops encoder and decoder blocks at fixed effective depth and applies a Poincaré-ball alignment loss at every iteration; Loop (6x2) beats the 12-layer base on WLASL2000 (64.73 vs 63.55 P-I), while aggressive sharing (4x3, 2x6) loses heavily.
key_contributions: Three looping designs compared (encoder-only, decoder-only, encoder-decoder); encoder-decoder looping best.
Progressive geometry-aware (hyperbolic) alignment applied at each loop iteration as auxiliary supervision.
Constant-effective-depth ablation (U x L) on WLASL.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: WLASL, MSASL skeleton data
setup.loops_train: fixed (U x L) with U*L constant (e.g., 6x2, 4x3, 2x6)
setup.baselines: 12-layer non-looped base; prior ISLR methods
setup.benchmarks: WLASL2000/300, MSASL1000 per-instance and per-class top-1

claims.claim: At constant effective depth, 6 unique layers x 2 loops beats the 12-layer base; 4x3 and 2x6 recover far more than same-size non-looped models but remain well below the base.
claims.evidence_quote: Most notably, Loop (6 × 2) achieves the highest overall scores (64.73 P-I, 62.41 P-C), surpassing the full 12-layer Base model.

claims.claim: Reducing unique layers without looping collapses accuracy (12x1 63.55 -> 6x1 23.17 P-I).
claims.evidence_quote: halving the 12-layer Base (12 × 1) drops P-I from 63.55 to 23.17, while Base (2 × 1) collapses entirely (0.13 P-I).

numbers.what: Loop (4x3) and (2x6) P-I
numbers.quote: P-I to 35.44 and 33.81, respectively, rescuing performance from their near-zero non-looped counterparts.

builds_on: Looped transformers (Giannou, Saunshi, Yang et al.)
survey_notes: Clean iso-effective-depth evidence that mild sharing (2 loops) can beat unique layers while aggressive sharing (3-6 loops of fewer layers) loses ~28 points; same pattern as bViT narrow width, ELT 1N x 32L, and LoopVLA's balanced L x N. Per-iteration auxiliary loss is a deep-supervision variant.

title: REIMU: Efficient Heterogeneous Hierarchical Reasoning for SSL-Based Speech Deepfake Detection
relevance_reason: Controlled comparison of single-pass, weight-shared recurrent, homogeneous HRM and heterogeneous HRM downstream backbones on SSL speech features.
one_sentence: REIMU systematically compares single-pass, weight-shared recurrent (2-3 passes), homogeneous HRM and heterogeneous HRM (self-attention + linear-attention modules) downstream of four SSL frontends for speech deepfake detection; recurrence and hierarchy alone do not help, heterogeneous operators do.
key_contributions: Controlled study disentangling recurrent computation, parameter sharing, and operator assignment for SSL-based deepfake detection.
Heterogeneous HRM with different high- and low-level operators; competitive with 10.8% fewer downstream parameters than the matched baseline.

setup.model_sizes: Base-scale SSL frontends (frozen) with small downstream backbones
setup.train_tokens_or_data: ASVspoof 2019 LA training
setup.loops_train: 2 or 3 recurrent passes; HRM schedules
setup.baselines: 6-layer single-pass backbones

claims.claim: Recurrence and hierarchical decomposition do not inherently improve detection; heterogeneous operator assignment is what helps.
claims.evidence_quote: show that recurrence and hierarchical decomposition do not inherently improve detection, whereas heterogeneous operator assignment provides a more competitive configuration.

claims.claim: The heterogeneous design remains competitive with 10.8% fewer downstream parameters than the matched baseline.
claims.evidence_quote: Notably, the heterogeneous design remains competitive while using 10.8% fewer downstream parameters than the matched baseline, demonstrating its potential for parameter-efficient speech deepfake detection.

survey_notes: Negative result for speech: plain weight-shared recurrence on SSL features does not improve deepfake detection. Contrasts with CoReLoop 2609.19818 (same task) where controlled recurrence inside the frozen SSL encoder helps; difference is where the loop sits and the added control modules.

title: ITS-Mina: A Harris Hawks Optimization-Based All-MLP Framework with Iterative Refinement and External Attention for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
relevance_reason: All-MLP forecaster that repeatedly applies a shared-parameter residual mixer stack (N iterations); looping is one of three components.
one_sentence: ITS-Mina combines a shared-parameter residual MLP mixer applied N times (N in {2,4,6,8} tuned), external attention with learnable memory, and Harris Hawks dropout tuning for multivariate time-series forecasting, reporting SOTA or competitive results on six benchmarks.
key_contributions: Iterative refinement by repeatedly applying a shared mixer stack.
External attention with learnable memory units at linear cost.
Metaheuristic (HHO) dropout tuning.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: six standard multivariate forecasting datasets
setup.loops_train: N time-mixing iterations in {2,4,6,8} (hyperparameter search)
setup.baselines: eleven forecasting models

claims.claim: Repeatedly applying a shared-parameter residual mixer stack deepens computation without more distinct parameters.
claims.evidence_quote: an iterative refinement mechanism that progressively enhances temporal representations by repeatedly applying a shared-parameter residual mixer stack, effectively deepening the model’s computational capacity without multiplying the number of distinct parameters

survey_notes: Peripheral time-series application; looping is not isolated from other components in the main comparison.

title: Time-multiplexed layer reuse for physical neural networks
relevance_reason: Cyclic reuse of a few weight banks across a deeper effective depth (time-multiplexed) for physical neural network hardware; interpolates between RNN and untied MLP.
one_sentence: TIDAL-Net time-multiplexes LW weight banks over LT effective layers to exploit fast forward dynamics but slow weight reconfiguration in physical neural networks; at fixed effective depth, error falls steeply with the first few extra unique banks and then flattens.
key_contributions: Hardware-motivated layer reuse for physical neural networks (fast dynamics, slow weight updates).
Sweep of unique weight banks LW at fixed effective depth LT on image classification and NLP.
Finding that splitting one large physical layer into smaller ones to add depth is often not beneficial under fixed parameter budgets.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: image classification (e.g., SVHN) and an NLP task (numerical simulation)
setup.loops_train: fixed LT effective layers with LW unique banks
setup.baselines: conventional PNN / untied multilayer limit / stateless RNN limit

claims.claim: At fixed effective depth, a few additional unique weight banks give most of the gain (reverse hockey-stick).
claims.evidence_quote: This shows that just a few additional sets of weights already provide a significant boost to the performance.

claims.claim: Under a fixed parameter budget, dividing one large layer into several smaller ones to increase effective depth is often not beneficial.
claims.evidence_quote: Therein we also find that “dividing” a single large trainable physical layer into multiple smaller layers in order to increase the effective depth is often not beneficial.

limitations: Numerical simulations; optimal LW/LT is task- and platform-specific.
builds_on: weight sharing in early digital NNs
survey_notes: Hardware/physical-computing angle: looping is motivated by slow weight reconfiguration (a memory-wall analogue). Width-over-depth finding at fixed params agrees with bViT 2605.10661.

title: Lightweight Bimodal Network for Single-Image Super-Resolution via Symmetric CNN and Recursive Transformer
relevance_reason: Super-resolution network with a Recursive Transformer module (transformer block applied recursively) alongside a CNN.
one_sentence: LBNet pairs a symmetric CNN for local features with a Recursive Transformer that refines texture via global attention; adding the recursive transformer raises PSNR/SSIM with small increases in multi-adds and runtime.
key_contributions: Hybrid lightweight SR network (Symmetric CNN + Recursive Transformer).
Claimed first use of recursion in a Transformer for SR.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: standard SR training sets
setup.loops_train: fixed recursion
setup.baselines: lightweight SISR methods
setup.benchmarks: Set5, Set14, BSDS100, Urban100, Manga109 PSNR/SSIM

claims.claim: Adding the Recursive Transformer improves PSNR/SSIM with an insignificant increase in multi-adds and execution time.
claims.evidence_quote: However, the increase in Multi-add and execution time is insignificant. In addition, the experiment also shows that the PSNR/SSIM results of the model with RT have been significantly improved.

survey_notes: Peripheral SR application; recursion not isolated from the transformer's addition. Lineage with DRCN 1511.04491.

title: Beyond Universal Transformer: block reusing with adaptor in Transformer for automatic speech recognition
relevance_reason: ASR Transformer with one encoder block reused 12 times and one decoder block reused 6 times, plus per-reuse adapter modules.
one_sentence: Reuses a single encoder block 12 times and a single decoder block 6 times in a CTC-attention ASR Transformer, adding small per-reuse adapters; on AISHELL-1 this cuts parameters from 29M to 7.6-8.3M at a CER cost (5.30% baseline vs 9.3% / 6.63% without / with adapters).
key_contributions: Block-reusing speech Transformer (BRST) at the same effective depth as the 12+6-block baseline.
Adapter module (ADM) per reuse giving a compact, adaptable model with few extra parameters.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: AISHELL-1
setup.loops_train: encoder block x12, decoder block x6
setup.baselines: 12-block encoder / 6-block decoder CTC-attention Transformer

claims.claim: Per-reuse adapters substantially recover the accuracy lost by pure block reuse at the same effective depth.
claims.evidence_quote: the proposed approach achieves the character error rate (CER) of 9.3%/6.63% with only 7.6M/8.3M parameters without and with the ADM, respectively.

numbers.what: baseline params (Mb) and CER for CTC greedy / prefix / attention / attention rescoring
numbers.quote: Model Params (Mb) CG CP ATT ATT-RE baseline 29 5.92 5.91 5.69 5.30

limitations: Pure block reuse loses substantial accuracy versus the unshared baseline.
survey_notes: Speech precursor of relaxed (adapter/LoRA) sharing: strict tying loses accuracy at iso-depth; per-step adapters close much of the gap (same direction as Relaxed Recursive Transformers in language and 2606.09357's unshared prelude/coda).

title: Recurrent Vision Transformer for Solving Visual Reasoning Problems
relevance_reason: CNN stem plus a transformer encoder applied recurrently (weight-shared in depth) with feedback until a stable prediction, for SVRT same-different reasoning.
one_sentence: RViT combines a convolutional stem with a recurrently applied (depth-tied) transformer encoder and feedback connections, reaching competitive SVRT same-different results with far fewer parameters and 28k training samples; harder problems need more pondering iterations.
key_contributions: Recurrent ViT with weight sharing in spatial and depth dimensions as a regularizer for low-data visual reasoning.
Ablations showing the importance of a hybrid CNN + transformer and of feedback connections.
Analysis of iterations: more challenging SVRT problems require more pondering steps.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: SVRT same-different problems, 28k training samples
setup.loops_train: recurrent iterations (depth tuned); optional probabilistic halting
setup.baselines: CNN baselines and non-recurrent transformer variants

claims.claim: Weight sharing in space and depth regularizes the model so it learns with far fewer free parameters from 28k samples.
claims.evidence_quote: The weight-sharing both in spatial and depth dimensions regularizes the model, allowing it to learn using far fewer free parameters, using only 28k training samples.

title: Attention is all you need for Videos: Self-attention based Video Summarization using Universal Transformers
relevance_reason: Student project applying Transformer and Universal Transformer to video captioning; UT used without ACT.

key_contributions: UT-based video captioning on precomputed 3D-CNN features.
Practical observation that ACT halts too early on video features.

setup.loops_train: 8 UT layers (fixed, ACT disabled)
setup.baselines: 6-layer Transformer

title: UCell: rethinking generalizability and scaling of bio-medical vision models
relevance_reason: Small (10-30M) single-cell segmentation model whose core ViT module is called recursively (N=21) with chunked, detached training and per-chunk supervision.
one_sentence: UCell recursively applies a ViT core 21 times for single-cell segmentation, training with the unrolled graph split into detached, separately supervised chunks; the 10-30M model matches models 10-20x larger and trains from scratch on microscopy data only.
key_contributions: Recursive ViT core (N=21) for parameter-efficient biomedical segmentation.
Chunked training: unrolled recursion split into chunks, earlier chunk outputs used as constant inputs (no gradient), each chunk supervised through the head.
Few-shot / one-shot adaptability and out-of-domain generalization without natural-image pretraining.

setup.loops_train: N=21 recursions split into 3 chunks

setup.benchmarks: single-cell segmentation F1/Dice on multiple benchmarks

claims.claim: A recursive 10-30M model matches models 10-20x larger with similar out-of-domain generalization.

claims.claim: Feature quality keeps improving over recursion iterations (decoded intermediate features).
claims.evidence_quote: Both the F1 scores (left panel) and Dice scores (right panel) demonstrated continued improvements of feature quality.

survey_notes: Biomedical vision; chunked detached training with per-chunk supervision is a hybrid of truncated BPTT and deep supervision (like TRM / RecycleNet). Data-scarce domain is the stated motivation for looping.

title: UCAN: Unified Convolutional Attention Network for Expansive Receptive Fields in Lightweight Super-Resolution
relevance_reason: Lightweight SR network that uses cross-layer parameter sharing as one of several efficiency components; looping not studied as such.
one_sentence: UCAN unifies window attention, Hedgehog attention and a distillation-based large-kernel module for lightweight super-resolution, and adds cross-layer parameter sharing to reduce complexity; reports 31.63 dB on Manga109 x4 at 48.4G MACs.
key_contributions: Hybrid convolution-attention SR network with expanded receptive field.
Cross-layer parameter sharing balanced with task-specific specialization.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: standard SR training sets
setup.baselines: lightweight SR models

claims.evidence_quote: In addition, we employ cross-layer parameter sharing to further reduce complexity. On Manga109 (4×), UCAN-L achieves 31.63 dB PSNR with only 48.4G MACs, surpassing recent lightweight models.

survey_notes: Peripheral; sharing is a compression add-on, not looping for compute. Low priority for the survey.

title: SMolLM: Small Language Models Learn Small Molecular Grammar
relevance_reason: 53K-parameter weight-shared transformer block looped D=8 times to generate SMILES, with mechanistic analysis across passes.

key_contributions: Weight-shared models dominate the sub-1M-parameter validity Pareto frontier for SMILES generation.
Mechanistic hierarchy across passes (brackets -> rings -> valence) from error classification, linear probing and SAE; bracket-matching head isolated by ablation.
Controls: unshared standard/modern GPTs and parameter-matched GRUs.

setup.model_sizes: WS-53K, WS-206K vs GPT-527K up to GPT-3.2M; GRU-53K
setup.train_tokens_or_data: ZINC-250K
setup.loops_train: virtual depth D=8 (also D4, D16 variants)
setup.baselines: unshared standard and modern GPT; parameter-matched GRU
setup.benchmarks: validity, uniqueness, novelty, internal diversity, FCD

claims.claim: A 53K weight-shared model beats a 10x larger unshared GPT in SMILES validity and matches its diversity.

claims.evidence_quote: WS-53K outperforms GPT-527K by 7.7 points (95.3% vs. 87.6%) and matches its internal diversity (0.852 vs. 0.851), at 10 times fewer parameters.

claims.evidence_quote: the same block resolves SMILES constraints across passes in a fixed hierarchy: brackets first, rings second, and valence last, as shown by error classification and linear probing

survey_notes: Chemistry/formal-language domain: tiny looped model beats 10x larger unshared GPT; useful mechanistic case of pass-wise algorithmic staging (cf. mechanistic looped-LM analyses). Scale is tiny (53K).

title: Vision Tiny Recursion Model (ViTRM): Parameter-Efficient Image Classification via Recursive State Refinement
relevance_reason: Replaces an L-layer ViT encoder with a TRM-style 3-layer block applied recursively N times with latent/answer states and deep supervision.
one_sentence: ViTRM applies a tiny 3-layer TRM-style block recursively for CIFAR classification; at ~3.6M parameters it is within 0.9 points of ViT-Small on CIFAR-10 (93.1 vs 94.0) and beats ResNets, and more recursion or supervision steps do not help.
key_contributions: TRM latent/answer recursion adapted to image classification with cross-attention from latent states to image tokens.
Comparisons against ViT-S/B/L and ResNets trained from scratch on CIFAR-10/100.
Ablations: minimal supervision depth (Nsup=1) best; diminishing returns beyond 3 latent steps.

setup.model_sizes: ~3.6M (4.7x fewer than ViT-Small, 23x fewer than ViT-Base)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 from scratch

claims.claim: ViTRM is within 0.9 points of ViT-Small on CIFAR-10 with 4.7x fewer parameters.
claims.regime: iso_data; parameters and compute not matched
claims.evidence_quote: On CIFAR-10, ViTRM achieves 93.1% accuracy (BS=128), within 0.9 percentage points of ViTSmall (94%) while using 4.7× fewer parameters.

claims.claim: More supervision steps overfit and latent depth beyond 3 gives diminishing returns.
claims.evidence_quote: We find that minimal supervision depth (Nsupervision =1) yields optimal performance, with excessive supervision leading to overfitting and degraded generalization.

limitations: Only low-resolution classification; no dense prediction.
survey_notes: TRM transfer to recognition: competitive at small scale, but recursion depth does not keep paying, agreeing with bViT 2605.10661 that recognition benefits saturate with loop count. Contrast with TRM's gains from deep supervision on puzzles: here more supervision steps overfit.

title: PRISM: Progressive Reasoning through Iterative Slot Memory for Vision
relevance_reason: Pyramid vision backbone with per-stage recurrent organize-recall-refine iterations (slots + VQ memory) and dynamic halting.

key_contributions: Organize-recall-refine recurrence per stage with object-centric slots and learned VQ memory.
Global dynamic halting per iteration (max 5 steps), allocating more steps to occluded inputs.
Evaluation on classification, detection and segmentation with occlusion robustness.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: ImageNet-1K; COCO; ADE20K
setup.loops_train: dynamic halting with Tmax=5
setup.baselines: feed-forward pyramid backbones of similar or larger size

claims.claim: More fixed recurrent steps improve occluded-input accuracy (saturating at 4-5), and dynamic halting beats fixed T=5.

title: Self-Critical Alternate Learning based Semantic Broadcast Communication
relevance_reason: Semantic broadcast communication built on a Universal Transformer codec; contribution is RL-based alternate training, not looping.

Self-critical RL with alternate learning to handle non-differentiable channels and semantic metrics.

claims.evidence_quote: we delve into multi-user broadcast communication (BC) based on the universal transformer (UT) and propose a reinforcement learning (RL) based self-critical alternate learning (SCAL) algorithm

title: Adaptive Length Image Tokenization via Recurrent Allocation
relevance_reason: Image tokenizer whose encoder-decoder is recurrently rolled out over iterations, refining 2D tokens and adding 1D latent tokens each iteration (abstract only).

Variable-length tokenization from 32 to 256 tokens.
Analysis showing token count aligns with entropy, familiarity and downstream requirements; signs of token specialization.

claims.claim: Token count aligns with image entropy, familiarity and downstream needs.
claims.evidence_quote: We validate our tokenizer using reconstruction loss and FID metrics, demonstrating that token count aligns with image entropy, familiarity and downstream task requirements.

title: A Recursively Recurrent Neural Network (R2N2) Architecture for Learning Iterative Algorithms
relevance_reason: Recursively recurrent superstructure (inner recurrent function evaluations, outer iterates) for meta-learning numerical iterative solvers (abstract only).

Learned iterations resemble classical Krylov, Newton-Krylov and Runge-Kutta solvers.

claims.claim: Training the superstructure on problem data yields iterations similar to classical iterative solvers.
claims.evidence_quote: yields iterations similar to Krylov solvers for linear equation systems, Newton-Krylov solvers for nonlinear equation systems, and Runge-Kutta integrators for ordinary differential equations.

survey_notes: Abstract only. Scientific-computing angle: recurrent structures learn known iterative algorithms, a counterpart to looped-transformer-as-algorithm theory.

title: Universal Transforming Geometric Network
relevance_reason: Replaces the RNN in the recurrent geometric network for protein structure prediction with a Universal Transformer encoder (abstract only).
one_sentence: UTGN uses the Universal Transformer encoder as the internal representation of an end-to-end differentiable protein structure predictor, improving over the RNN-based RGN by 1.7 Å (free modeling) and 0.7 Å (template-based) on CASP12 (abstract only).

claims.claim: UTGN improves over RGN on CASP12 free modeling and template-based modeling.
claims.evidence_quote: Our experiments show that compared to RGN, UTGN achieve a $1.7$ \si{\angstrom} improvement on the free modeling portion and a $0.7$ \si{\angstrom} improvement on the template based modeling of the CASP12 competition.

survey_notes: Abstract only. Early science-domain use of the UT; the gain is relative to an RNN, not to an unshared transformer, so it says little about looping per se.

title: Rethinking Depth: A study of the Recursive-Transformer for Speech Recognition
relevance_reason: Systematic study of weight-tied depth recursion (plain and prelude-recurrent-coda) in ASR encoders at matched effective depth.
one_sentence: On LibriSpeech, a 24-effective-layer ASR encoder with a looped middle block (2 prelude + 4 shared layers x5 + 2 coda) keeps WER near the 24-unique-layer baseline with 66% fewer encoder parameters; a parameter-matched looped variant beats the baseline.
key_contributions: Layer-similarity analysis of the Whisper-medium encoder shows redundant middle layers, motivating a prelude/recurrent/coda split for ASR encoders.

Controlled sweep of {nr, L, np, nc} at a fixed 24 processed layers (same FLOPs): plain recursion degrades gracefully down to 1 layer x24; adding 2 unshared prelude and coda layers recovers most of the gap.
Loop-count study: 5 loops best, more loops hurt at fixed unique layers; a loop-count curriculum (1 to 20) helps test-clean; gains concentrate on hard and long utterances.

setup.model_sizes: encoder 3.1M-75.6M (decoder 24 layers, not counted); Branchformer 33.6M-101.6M; AISHELL-1 7.8M-15.7M
setup.train_tokens_or_data: LibriSpeech 960 h; AISHELL-1 150 h; 60 epochs, CTC+Seq2Seq loss
setup.loops_train: fixed L per run (2 to 24); also length-proportional L (1-20) and curriculum 1->20
setup.baselines: 24-unique-layer Transformer encoder (75.6M); Branchformer; AISHELL-1 12-layer Transformer

claims.claim: At a fixed 24 processed layers (same FLOPs), plain recursion trades WER for parameters: 12x2 is near-lossless at -50% parameters, 1x24 degrades to 2.78 (6.49) at -95%.
claims.evidence_quote: When nr is reduced and L increased (configurations R1 and R2), WER rises slightly to 2.15% (5.03%) and 2.25% (5.23%), while parameter counts drop to 37.8M and 18.9M, respectively.

claims.claim: Adding unshared prelude and coda layers (Latent-Recursive) improves over plain recursion at similar parameter counts.
claims.evidence_quote: These results demonstrate that augmenting RecursiveTransformer architectures with latent non-shared layers consistently improves recognition performance, highlighting the advantages of the Latent-Recursive design.

claims.claim: A parameter-matched looped encoder (20 shared layers x5 plus 2+2, more FLOPs) beats the 24-layer baseline.
claims.evidence_quote: We further evaluated a Latent-Recursive configuration (L3, {20,5,2,2}) with the same number of parameters as baseline B, achieving 2.03% (4.73%) WER, surpassing standard Transformers B under parameter-matched settings.

claims.claim: Loop count has an optimum (5); 10 and 20 loops degrade at fixed unique layers.
claims.evidence_quote: However, increasing the number of loops beyond this degraded performance. For example, L110 and L120 resulted in WERs of 2.18% (4.94%) and 2.31% (5.30%), respectively.

numbers.what: baseline 24-layer encoder WER test-clean (test-other), params
numbers.quote: It achieves a word error rate (WER) of 2.12% (4.76%), for testclean and test-other respectively, with 75.6M parameters.

numbers.what: single layer looped 24 times
numbers.quote: R4, comprising a single layer looped 24 times, records the highest WER of 2.78% (6.49%) with only 3.1M parameters (a 95% reduction).

numbers.what: no recurrence (L=1) in L1 config
numbers.quote: The L11 configuration, corresponding to a single pass through block R (no recurrence), produced the weakest performance, with WERs of 2.44% (test-clean) and 5.63% (test-other)

numbers.what: Branchformer looped variant vs baseline
numbers.quote: the Branchformer baseline (B3) records 1.97% and 4.86% WER on test-clean and test-other, respectively, whereas the Latent-Recursive Branchformer (L5) achieves 2.04% and 4.62% with 66% fewer parameters.

numbers.what: Latent-Recursive L1 {4,5,2,2} and L2 {1,20,2,2} WER and params
numbers.quote: Modified versions of R3 and R4, denoted L1 and L2 respectively, achieve WERs of 2.16% (4.92%) and 2.31% (5.30%) with parameter counts of 25.2M and 15.7M, respectively (Table 1).

numbers.what: loop sweep L=2 and L=5 in L1 config
numbers.quote: Introducing two loops (L12 ) improved performance to 2.23% and 5.12%, while five loops (L1) yielded the best results: 2.16% and 4.92%.

numbers.what: headline parameter reduction
numbers.quote: especially when recurrence is applied in the latent space with a restricted number of loops, obtaining comparable performance while reducing the parameter count by 66%.

limitations: Fixed loop count only (no adaptive halting); encoder-only study with a fixed 24-layer decoder; max 101.6M encoder; loops beyond 5 degrade.
survey_notes: Clean iso-effective-depth evidence in speech: the language finding that middle layers are redundant and prelude/coda should stay unshared transfers to ASR encoders. Unlike Huginn-style LMs, loops beyond the training count were not explored, and more loops at train time hurt beyond 5 (contrast with LoopMDM 2605.26106 where more inference loops help). Reported 'same FLOPs' configurations are effectively iso-effective-depth.

title: Multimodal Latent Reasoning via Hierarchical Visual Cues Injection
relevance_reason: Builds a multimodal LLM on the Huginn-3.5B recurrent-depth backbone and injects hierarchical ViT features into the recurrent iterations.
one_sentence: HIVE extends Huginn-3.5B into an MLLM, injecting multi-level ViT features (global to regional) into early recurrent iterations with an adaptive schedule; accuracy rises steeply with test-time recurrence (ScienceQA-img 32.82% at r=1 to 91.57% at r=32) and saturates beyond 32.
key_contributions: First multimodal extension of the Huginn recurrent-depth LM, trained with Huginn's log-normal Poisson recurrence sampling and truncated backprop.
Hierarchical visual cue injection into the latent recurrence, with an adaptive schedule depending on whether R >= 4 or R < 4.
Test-time scaling and adaptive early exit in the multimodal setting: hierarchical cues reduce average recurrence steps to exit (e.g., 25.4 -> 18.1 on MMBench).

setup.train_tokens_or_data: LLaVA-style multi-stage training (ShareGPT4V, ALLaVA, etc.)
setup.loops_train: recurrence sampled from log-normal Poisson with mean 32
setup.loops_test: r = 1..64; adaptive early exit with max r=32
setup.baselines: same setup trained with r=1 (non-recurrent), recurrent without hierarchical cues; other LMM backbones (Gemma3, LLaMA2, Phi-3-mini)

claims.claim: Test-time recurrence drives large gains: the hierarchical model rises from 32.82% at r=1 to 91.57% at r=32 on ScienceQA-img, while a model trained with r=1 stays near 59%.
claims.evidence_quote: For instance, the hierarchical model climbs from 32.82% at r = 1 to a peak of 91.57% at r = 32, validating that iterative recurrence allows the model to progressively refine its internal representations.

claims.claim: Returns diminish beyond r=32 (91.57% -> 91.27% at r=64).
claims.evidence_quote: The performance gains for the hierarchical model plateau, moving from 91.57% (r = 32) to a slight fluctuation at 91.27% (r = 64).

claims.claim: Hierarchical cues give modest accuracy gains and faster exit under adaptive compute.
claims.evidence_quote: Concretely, the mean reasoning steps decrease from 25.4 to 18.1 on MMBench, 24.9 to 17.7 on MMStar, and 24.8 to 17.0 on ScienceQAimg .

numbers.what: ScienceQA-img at r=32 with vs without hierarchical cues
numbers.quote: At the recurrence depth of r = 32, the full model reaches 91.57%, compared with 89.39%

numbers.what: non-recurrent (r=1-trained) baseline average across steps on ScienceQA-img
numbers.quote: While the non-recurrent baseline remains stagnant at a low performance level (averaging 59.0% across all steps), both recurrent variants exhibit a dramatic upward trajectory as r increases.

limitations: Authors note room for tuning and resolution settings for OCR/document tasks; saturation beyond r=32.
survey_notes: Direct transfer of the Huginn recipe (randomized Poisson recurrence, truncated BPTT, KV-based early exit) to vision-language; test-time recurrence scaling persists with visual inputs. Caution: the r=1 accuracy (32.82%) is far below the r=1-trained baseline (~59%), i.e., the looped model is poor at low compute, like Huginn and LoopMDM at S=1. The 'non-recurrent baseline' starts from a recurrent backbone, so this is not a clean dense-vs-looped comparison; external backbone comparisons are unmatched.

title: Déjà View: Looping Transformers for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction
relevance_reason: Single shared, time-conditioned transformer block looped K times over DINOv2 per-view tokens for feed-forward 3D reconstruction; K is an inference compute knob.
one_sentence: A 117M-parameter model loops one gated, time-interval-conditioned frame/global attention block K in [8,16] times on DINOv2 tokens; it matches or beats much larger feed-forward 3D reconstruction models, and shared weights beat 16 untied blocks at matched data and compute.
key_contributions: Looped multi-view reconstruction transformer: DINOv2 ViT-B encoder, one shared frame+global attention block with RAPTOR-style residual and state gates conditioned on continuous time interval (t_k, t_k+1), shallow depth/ray decoders; supervised only at the final step.
Variable-K training (K ~ Beta(2,1) on [8,16]) gives one checkpoint usable at several budgets within about 2-3% of fixed-K models.

Analysis: the recurrence does not reach a fixed point (state norm grows) but its direction converges ('directional refinement'); weight-shared block beats a decoupled 16-block variant with 16x more parameters.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: multi-view 3D datasets, 2-18 views at 504 px, ~2.5M tokens per step, 128 H100s; ablations 100K iterations on same data
setup.loops_train: K ~ Beta(2,1) scaled to [8,16]
setup.baselines: MASt3R, MASt3R-SfM, MapAnything, Pi3, VGGT, VGGT-Omega-1B, DA3-L/G (public checkpoints); decoupled 16-block variant (ablation)
setup.benchmarks: DTU, ETH3D, 7-Scenes, ScanNet++, nuScenes pointmap Rel. L2 / inlier ratio, pose AUC@3/@30

claims.claim: Against public feed-forward models with up to 10x more parameters, the looped 117M model matches or exceeds them at comparable or lower compute.
claims.evidence_quote: At 117M parameters and 75.9 TFLOPs of compute (Table 3), DéjàView matches or exceeds much larger feed-forward methods while running in under 5 GiB of peak memory at 24 input views.

claims.claim: Weight sharing alone beats an otherwise identical decoupled model with 16 independent blocks, at same data and compute; gates add further gains.
claims.evidence_quote: Notably, weight sharing alone already outperforms the decoupled architecture despite having 16× fewer parameters.

claims.claim: Variable-K training matches fixed-K training at each budget (within ~2-3%) but does not exceed it, and the recurrence does not extrapolate beyond Kmax.
claims.evidence_quote: First, the trained recurrence does not extrapolate beyond its step range: a few channels diverge once Kinf exceeds Kmax .

claims.claim: The recurrence is not a fixed-point iteration: state norm grows while direction converges to the endpoint.
claims.evidence_quote: Unlike deep equilibrium networks [Bai et al., 2019], our recurrence does not converge to a fixed point in feature space. Instead, the state norm ∥zk ∥ grows monotonically with k.

numbers.what: Block ablation averages (Rel. L2 / IR / AUC@3 / AUC@30): decoupled vs shared vs full
Variable-K vs fixed K=16 at K_inf=16
numbers.quote: At Kinf =16, variable-K training matches Fixed K=16 within ∼2% on every metric.

numbers.what: Pi3 competitor size and compute relative to DéjàView
numbers.quote: Pi3 [Wang et al., 2025b] is the closest competitor, leading on indoor pointmap accuracy at 8× our parameters and 2× our compute.

numbers.what: relative update norm decay across iterations
numbers.quote: the relative update magnitude ∥∆zk ∥/∥zk ∥ decays from ∼ 0.5 at the first step to ∼ 0.1 at the last

numbers.what: VGGT parameter ratio relative to DéjàView
numbers.quote: VGGT [Wang et al., 2025] retains its lead on DTU pose at 10× our parameters, with its lead concentrated at the tightest AUC@3◦ threshold (96.5 vs 83.2)

limitations: No extrapolation beyond trained Kmax (channels diverge); variable-K only matches fixed-K; no dynamic scenes.
builds_on: RAPTOR (Jacobs et al. 2026, looped ViT distillation)
Yang et al. 2024 looped transformer stabilization
survey_notes: Strongest vision evidence that weight-shared iteration is an inductive bias, not only a parameter saver: shared block beats a 16x larger untied stack at matched data and compute (iso-effective-depth). Headline SOTA comparisons are unmatched (public checkpoints). Contradiction with language results on loop extrapolation (Huginn, LoopMDM 2605.26106 extrapolate past training max; DéjàView diverges past Kmax). Uses continuous-time interval conditioning (like flow/ODE steps) rather than discrete step embedding. Final-step-only supervision, unlike RAFT sequence losses.

title: RD-ViT: Recurrent-Depth Vision Transformer for Semantic Segmentation with Reduced Data Dependence Extending the Recurrent-Depth Transformer Architecture to Dense Prediction
relevance_reason: Single shared ViT block looped T=8 times (prelude/coda) with LTI-stable state injection, ACT halting, depth-wise LoRA and optional MoE, for cardiac MRI segmentation.
one_sentence: RD-ViT loops one shared block 8 times with LTI-stable input injection, ACT and per-depth LoRA on ACDC cardiac segmentation; it beats a same-effective-depth ViT with unique layers in 2D (also at 10% data) and extrapolates to more loops without degradation.
key_contributions: Transfers the recurrent-depth transformer recipe (LTI-stable injection with spectral radius < 1, ACT, depth-wise LoRA, MoE FFN) to 2D/3D dense prediction.
Same-effective-depth comparison against a 10-layer unique-weight ViT (2.2x params) including a 10%-data regime.
Stable depth extrapolation (T=10-16 after training at T=8) and ACT ponder time decreasing during training.

setup.model_sizes: RD-ViT Tiny (standard ViT baseline has ~2.2x its parameters); 3D MoE variant 3.0M
setup.train_tokens_or_data: ACDC cardiac MRI (100 patient volumes), full and 10% data
setup.loops_train: T=8 with ACT
setup.baselines: standard ViT with same effective depth (1+8+1=10 unique layers)

claims.claim: At the same effective depth, RD-ViT beats a unique-weight ViT in 2D at both 10% and full data.
claims.evidence_quote: In 2D, RD-ViT outperforms standard ViT at 10% training data (Dice 0.774 vs 0.762) and at full data (0.882 vs 0.872).

claims.claim: Inference with more loops than training (T=10-16 vs 8) is stable, attributed to the LTI-stable injection.
claims.evidence_quote: When we increase iterations beyond the training depth (T=10, 12, 16), performance remains stable at 0.77 with no degradation.

numbers.what: 3D RD-ViT+MoE vs standard ViT Dice
numbers.quote: In 3D, RD-ViT with MoE achieves Dice 0.812 with 3.0M parameters, reaching 99.4% of standard ViT performance (0.817) at 53% of the parameter count.

numbers.what: baseline construction: same effective depth, unique weights
numbers.quote: The Standard ViT baseline uses the same total effective depth (prelude + loop iterations + coda = 1 + 8 + 1 = 10 layers) but with unique weights per layer, resulting in approximately 2.2× the parameters of RD-ViT Tiny.

limitations: Small single benchmark (ACDC); small models; Colab-scale experiments.
survey_notes: Medical segmentation transfer of the LM recurrent-depth recipe; small-data regime motivates sharing as regularization (same argument as ELT's UCF-101 and GET). Extrapolation is stable but saturates (no gain beyond trained T), unlike LoopMDM where extra loops keep improving. Evidence is small-scale and single-dataset.
